handoff: AC1–AC8 met and green (unit, typecheck, slice integration). Blocking F1: a forced round receipt rejected for a changed workflow file overwrites the unfinished round's gate/ask/stuck park with a workflow park (decide/story.ts roundStart); needs a fix and an S1 test. Nits F2, F3.

findings.title: A forced round whose workflow file changed before the tick loses its gate/ask park
findings.detail:
roundStart rejects a hash mismatch with state `{ ...moved, park: { kind: "workflow", ... } }` (rule round.workflow_changed). Before this slice only finished rounds reached it (`!r.forced && !roundFinished(st)` rejects earlier), so overwriting `park` on a $done round was harmless and the comment says 'the round stays finished'. Now a forced receipt on an unfinished round reaches the same line: e.g. gh-71 parked at triage's `confirm` gate → `norn story edit gh-71 --workflow story --force` → someone edits .agents/workflows/story.yaml before the tick → the tick leaves round 1 at `confirm`, status parked, but with park.kind `workflow` instead of `gate`. The gate (or an agent's ask, or a stuck reason) is gone: `story approve`/`story answer` on it no longer apply, and the only way out is re-running the forced edit. The spec says a rejected round receipt changes nothing about the round (D1: 'the receipt is rejected into the trace with an inbox item to run the edit again'; B17/AC8 'the unfinished round is untouched'). No test covers the forced + workflow-changed case.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: On an unfinished (forced) round keep its own park: reject with `moved` and surface the 'run it again' item without replacing the park (or only set the workflow park when roundFinished(st)). Add an S1 test: forced edit at a gate, change the workflow file, tick → round still parked at the gate (approve still works) and the inbox asks for the edit again.

findings.title: `st.step as string` hides that `ended.at` is a StepName
findings.detail:
`ended: { by: "person", at: st.step as string, ... }` casts away `$done`; UnitState.ended.at is StepName (no `$done`). Today an unfinished round is never at $done, so it holds, but the cast silences the type checker if that changes and the write would fail schema validation (S2 corrupt).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Narrow instead of casting (e.g. take `r.left_at`, which the stale check already pins to st.step, with a guard), or let the type prove it.

findings.title: `--force` on a slice target is accepted and silently ignored
findings.detail:
editWorkflow passes `force` only to the story-round branch; `norn story edit gh-71/02 --workflow quick --at implement --force` runs the in-place slice switch with no sign the flag did nothing. The spec scopes --force to stories (RD3).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Refuse or usage-error `--force` on a slice target, or say so in the option help.
